title: Model Context Protocol (MCP) | Intercom and Fin Developer Platform
snippet:
Region availability
The Intercom MCP server is available for US and EU hosted workspaces. AU hosted workspaces are not yet supported. Connect using the endpoint that matches your workspace's hosted region — see the connection URLs below.

Intercom hosts a remote MCP server that follows the authenticated remote MCP specification ([docs](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-03-26/basic/authorization)). This server handles requests from AI tools and provides access to Intercom data through a secure interface.
**Connection URLs:**
Use the endpoint for your workspace's hosted region. You can tell your region from your workspace URL: `app.intercom.com` is US hosted and `app.eu.intercom.com` is EU hosted.
| Region | Streamable HTTP (Recommended) | Legacy SSE (deprecated) |
|---|---|---|
| US | `https://mcp.intercom.com/mcp` | `https://mcp.intercom.com/sse` |
| EU | `https://mcp.eu.intercom.com/mcp` | `https://mcp.eu.intercom.com/sse` |
Requests to the EU endpoint are processed within the EU, in line with Intercom's [Regional Data Hosting](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/6124430-regional-data-hosting) commitments.
When an AI tool or application needs to access Intercom data:
1. The tool connects to Intercom's MCP server
2. Authentication verifies the user's permissions
3. The tool can then access relevant Intercom data and functionality
4. The connection remains live to receive updates as needed

The Intercom MCP Server provides **14 tools** for interacting with the Intercom API. Workspaces with Fin Operator also get the [Fin Operator tools](/docs/guides/mcp#fin-operator-tools).
### Universal Tools
---
#### **search**
Universal search tool for finding conversations and contacts using a query DSL approach.
**Key Features:**
- **Must specify** `object_type:conversations` or `object_type:contacts` to indicate which API to call
- Supports complex field-based queries with operators (eq, neq, gt, lt, contains, etc.)
- Returns summary results with IDs prefixed by type (`conversation_*` or `contact_*`)
- Built-in pagination support with `starting_after` parameter
- Free-text search capability with `q:` parameter
**Example Queries:**

1. **OAuth Flow (Recommended)**: Browser-based authentication with a consent step, described below
2. **Bearer Token**: Direct API token authentication

title: intercom.com/integrations/connectors/intercom-mcp-server
snippet:
Intercom's MCP server lets AI tools and CLIs (like Claude Code, Claude Desktop, ChatGPT, Cursor, and VS Code) securely access your Intercom data through the Model Context Protocol. Query conversations, contacts, companies, and Help Center articles, and create or update articles directly from your AI tool. Available for US-hosted Intercom workspaces.
## What you can do
-   Connect via the Streamable HTTP endpoint at https://mcp.intercom.com/mcp
-   Read conversations, contacts, and companies; read and write Help Center articles
-   Works with MCP-compatible clients including Claude Code, Claude Desktop, ChatGPT, Cursor, and VS Code
-   Authenticate with OAuth, scoped to your existing Intercom permissions
-   Available for US-hosted Intercom workspaces
## How it works
Add the Intercom MCP server to your AI tool using the Streamable HTTP endpoint https://mcp.intercom.com/mcp. Available for US-hosted Intercom workspaces.
Authenticate with OAuth to grant access scoped to your existing Intercom permissions. Works with MCP-compatible clients including Claude Code, Claude Desktop, ChatGPT, Cursor, and VS Code.
Once connected, query conversations, contacts, companies, and Help Center articles, and create or update articles directly from your AI tool.
## Configure
The Intercom MCP server provides read access to conversations, contacts, and companies, plus read and write access to Help Center articles. Currently available for US-hosted workspaces only.

title: Fin Agent API: MCP Server
snippet:
The Fin Agent API exposes a remote [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server that lets external AI agents call Fin as a tool. Instead of rebuilding support logic in your own agent, you can plug in Fin’s knowledge base, procedures, and multi-turn conversation capabilities directly from within any MCP-compatible client, including Claude, Claude Code, Cursor, or your own agent framework.
# Use cases
The Fin Agent API MCP server is designed for multi-agent scenarios where your own agent needs access to Fin’s capabilities:
- **Embedded support in product agents.** Give your product’s AI assistant the ability to answer support questions using your configured Fin knowledge, without duplicating your knowledge base or content.
- **Procedure automation.** Let an orchestrating agent trigger Fin procedures (refunds, upgrades, cancellations) on behalf of users and handle multi-turn interactions programmatically.
- **Capability-driven routing.** Use list_fin_capabilities to determine what actions are available for a given user, then route to the right tool in your agent’s decision logic.
- **Developer tooling.** Surface your Fin knowledge inside developer tools like Claude Code or Cursor, so internal users can query your support content from their existing workflow.

# Endpoint
```
https://api.intercom.io/fin/mcp
```
Use this when a trusted backend service is calling Fin on behalf of a user. The caller authenticates with the Fin Agent API key for the workspace. The end-user identity is supplied in the request body by the calling service. This model is appropriate for server-to-server integrations where your backend controls who is making the request.
# Authentication
Pass your Fin Agent API api key as a Bearer token in the Authorization header:
```
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_FIN_AGENT_API_KEY
```
# Connecting from Claude
## Claude Desktop
Add the following to your claude_desktop_config.json:
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"fin": {
"command": "npx",
"args": [
"-y",
"mcp-remote",
"https://api.intercom.io/fin/mcp",
"--header",
"Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_FIN_AGENT_API_KEY}"
}
}
}
}
```
## Claude Code (CLI)
```
claude mcp add intercom-fin \
--transport http \
https://api.intercom.io/fin/mcp \
--header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_FIN_AGENT_API_KEY"
```

Once connected, the MCP server exposes five tools to the client.

title: plugins/third_party/intercom/README.md at main · cursor/plugins
snippet:
Cursor plugin that connects agents to [Intercom](https://www.intercom.com) through Intercom's official remote [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) server.
Search conversations and contacts, look up companies, and list, search, create, or update Help Center articles in the signed-in Intercom workspace.

## MCP
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"intercom": {
"type": "http",
"url": "https://mcp.intercom.com/mcp"
}
}
}
```
Auth is OAuth 2.0 against Intercom with Dynamic Client Registration (DCR) and PKCE. Cursor registers itself and prompts for Intercom sign-in when the plugin connects — there is no API key or client ID to configure.
## Regions
This plugin points at the US endpoint. Intercom MCP is available for US and EU hosted workspaces; AU is not supported yet.
| Region | Workspace URL | MCP URL |
|---|---|---|
| US | `app.intercom.com` | `https://mcp.intercom.com/mcp` |
| EU | `app.eu.intercom.com` | `https://mcp.eu.intercom.com/mcp` |
If your workspace is EU-hosted, change the `url` in `mcp.json` to `https://mcp.eu.intercom.com/mcp` after install.

- Server URL (US): [https://mcp.intercom.com/mcp](https://mcp.intercom.com/mcp)

title: intercom-mcp-server/README.md at main · intercom/intercom-mcp-server
snippet:
Region availability Currently the Intercom MCP server is only supported in US hosted workspaces.
## What is Model Context Protocol?
MCP is a protocol that enables AI tools and applications to connect with Intercom's data and services in a secure, standardized way. It provides a structured method for AI models to:
- Find and retrieve Intercom data (conversations, contacts, etc.)
- Access specific tools and functionality provided by Intercom
- Maintain context about your Intercom workspace when working with AI assistants
## How MCP Works
Intercom hosts a remote MCP server that follows the authenticated remote MCP specification ([docs](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-03-26/basic/authorization)). This server handles requests from AI tools and provides access to Intercom data through a secure interface.
**Connection URLs:**
- **Streamable HTTP (Recommended)**: `https://mcp.intercom.com/mcp`
- **Legacy SSE**: `https://mcp.intercom.com/sse` (deprecated, maintained for backwards compatibility)
When an AI tool or application needs to access Intercom data:
1. The tool connects to Intercom's MCP server
2. Authentication verifies the user's permissions
3. The tool can then access relevant Intercom data and functionality
4. The connection remains live to receive updates as needed

#### **search**
Universal search tool for finding conversations and contacts using a query DSL approach.
**Key Features:**
- **Must specify** `object_type:conversations` or `object_type:contacts` to indicate which API to call
- Supports complex field-based queries with operators (eq, neq, gt, lt, contains, etc.)
- Returns summary results with IDs prefixed by type (`conversation_*` or `contact_*`)
- Built-in pagination support with `starting_after` parameter
- Free-text search capability with `q:` parameter

### Authentication Methods
The MCP server supports **two authentication approaches**:
1. **OAuth Flow (Recommended)**: Automatic browser-based authentication
2. **Bearer Token**: Direct API token authentication

For **OAuth authentication** (recommended):
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"intercom": {
"command": "npx",
"args": [
"mcp-remote",
"https://mcp.intercom.com/mcp"
]
}
}
}
```
For **Bearer token authentication**:
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"intercom": {
"command": "npx",
"args": [
"mcp-remote",
"https://mcp.intercom.com/mcp",
"--header",
"Authorization:${AUTH_HEADER}"
],
"env": {
"AUTH_HEADER": "Bearer YOUR_INTERCOM_API_TOKEN"
}
}
}
}
```

title: Intercom MCP server, what its 14 tools can do
snippet:
[Intercom](https://heydeacon.com/resources/intercom-pricing) has an official [MCP server](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/guides/mcp) that lets Claude, ChatGPT, [Claude Code](https://heydeacon.com/resources/lovable-vs-claude-code) or [Cursor](https://heydeacon.com/resources/cursor-alternatives) search your Intercom conversations, contacts, companies and Help Center articles. You add `https://mcp.intercom.com/mcp` to your AI tool, or `https://mcp.eu.intercom.com/mcp` if your workspace is hosted in the EU, and sign in through your browser. It has 14 tools. Three of them write, creating and editing Help Center articles and adding internal notes, and none of them can send a reply your customer sees. Australian workspaces can’t use it yet, and Intercom doesn’t say which plans include it.

Intercom’s [docs](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/guides/mcp) split them into two universal tools and 12 that map onto its API. Signing in gives your AI tool access [scoped to your existing Intercom permissions](https://www.intercom.com/integrations/connectors/intercom-mcp-server), so it sees what you see in the inbox.

An EU workspace has a few traps. Intercom’s connector in Claude’s directory only connects to US workspaces. Connecting a US address to an EU workspace gets you “We’re having technical difficulties” after you press Allow, and the fix is to remove the connection and add it again with the EU address. And Intercom’s [integration page](https://www.intercom.com/integrations/connectors/intercom-mcp-server) still says the server is for US-hosted workspaces only, while its developer docs and its [help centre](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/11461635-add-mcp-connectors-for-popular-apps-or-custom-mcps) both give the EU address, so go by those two.
## Connecting Claude
These are Intercom’s [steps for Claude](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/guides/mcp), with the button names from [Claude’s help centre](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11176164-use-connectors-to-extend-claude-s-capabilities).
1. For a US workspace, open Customize in Claude, then Connectors, press the + next to Connectors, pick Intercom and press Connect.
2. For an EU workspace, add it as a custom connector instead. Open Customize, then Connectors, press Add, choose Custom, then Web, give it a name and paste `https://mcp.eu.intercom.com/mcp`.
3. On Claude Team or Enterprise, an Owner adds it first under Organization settings, then Connectors, and each person then signs in.
